sections.h2: What should a Corpus Christi owner consider before choosing a sale route?
sections.html:
Condition and timing carry the most weight. A well kept house can do well in a listing, while a storm-damaged, inherited or rented one often moves faster to a buyer who takes it as it stands.

The Texas State Historical Association calls Corpus Christi a seaport at the mouth of the Nueces River on the west end of Corpus Christi Bay, the county seat of Nueces County and the largest city on the South Texas coast. It sits where Interstate 37 meets U.S. highways 77 and 181, 210 miles southwest of Houston. Salt air, wind and storm history make roofs, windows and foundations the first things coastal buyers check.

  • Open listing: widest reach for a house that shows well.
  • Owner sale: no commission, more paperwork for you.
  • Cash purchase: quicker and as-is, useful after storm damage or for an estate.

sections.h2: How did hurricanes and the port shape Corpus Christi?
sections.html:
A hurricane on September 14, 1919 destroyed much of the North Beach area and the central business district and killed some 350 to 400 people, according to the Handbook of Texas. The city then pushed for a deepwater port, which opened on September 14, 1926.

The port brought rapid growth: the population more than doubled from 10,522 in 1920 to 27,741 in 1930. Oil was found in the county in 1930, and the Naval Air Station and refineries became pillars of the economy. The Handbook also lists Padre Island National Seashore and the bay among recreation draws, along with Del Mar College and Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi.

Source: Handbook of Texas, Corpus Christi. Keep storm repair receipts and insurance claim records, since buyers and lenders will ask about that past.

sections.h2: What are Corpus Christi's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
The city defines a short-term rental as renting all or part of a residential unit for less than 30 days and not less than 12 hours, and it requires registration for any property rented that way. Permits are valid for the calendar year and renewed each January.

The ordinance approved on June 28, 2022 allows rentals with restrictions in single-family districts citywide, but not in single-family districts within the Padre and Mustang Island area plan. Type 1 means the owner or operator lives there; Type 2 means no one does, and Type 2 rentals were limited to 15 percent of a block face, first come first served. Hotel occupancy tax filing applies to short-term rentals, hotels and bed and breakfasts.

A later city news release described a moratorium on new Type 1 permits through November 17, 2026, with staff to bring changes to council on or before that date, and said permits valid through December 31, 2026 would stay active. It also directed staff to apply the density limit to renewals, with at least one Type 2 rental per block face. Rules may have changed since, so ask Development Services for the current version.

  • Applications ask for owner and agent contacts, a floor plan with sleeping areas, a guest maximum and exits, and a 24-hour contact person.
  • The printed permit fee was $250 for 2023; ask the city for the current fee.
  • Development Services is at (361) 826-3240.

Sources: city short-term rental page and council action release. Do not tell a buyer a permit transfers with the house unless the city confirms it.

sections.h2: Where do Corpus Christi deeds and tax records live?
sections.html:
City parcels in Nueces County are filed at the Nueces County clerk, and the appraisal district for that county sets values. Addresses near the city edge can lie in a neighboring county, so your latest tax bill is the quickest check.

The courts' clerk manual says a deed needs an acknowledgment or two witnesses to be accepted for filing. It prices a first page at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, with extra charges for names beyond five and for records funds. Ask the clerk for today's schedule; your title company usually handles the filing.

Reference: county clerk manual.

sections.h2: What happens if property taxes on a Corpus Christi home go unpaid?
sections.html:
A bill unpaid after January 31 is delinquent as of February 1. Interest of one percent a month starts then, a six percent penalty applies at the outset, and by July 1 the penalty reaches 12 percent. A taxing unit's attorney may add up to 20 percent on top.

The lien that secures each year's tax attaches on January 1 and follows the house through a sale, so a buyer cannot obtain clear title until back taxes are cleared. At closing the title company pays what you owe out of your proceeds. Seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans may use installments, and some collectors offer payment plans up to 36 months on a homestead.

Pages: paying property taxes and deadlines.

sections.h2: What if the Corpus Christi house is tied up in a land contract or has an occupant?
sections.html:
A contract for deed, also called an installment land contract, keeps title with the seller until the buyer pays in full, and Texas Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D governs those for residences. The purchaser has a statutory right to cancel under that law, so get legal advice before selling a house under such a contract.

If someone stays after being told to leave, an owner may ask the sheriff or constable for removal under Property Code chapter 24B, but only when conditions are met, including that the occupant is not a family member or a current or former tenant. Wrongful removal can lead to a lawsuit. Otherwise, the usual route is an eviction suit in justice court.

Sources: the Attorney General's opinion on executory contracts and the State Law Library eviction guide.

sections.h2: What should a Corpus Christi seller gather before an offer?
sections.html:
Pull together the deed, loan payoff, tax bill, insurance claim history and permits for any storm work. Coastal buyers raise flood and wind coverage early, so know what your policy covers and which company writes it.

Line up offers by net proceeds and by weeks to closing. A cash buyer may close sooner and will price in repairs; a listing may net more after a longer wait. Have each buyer state in writing who pays title, recording and the tax split.

faqs.q: Is Corpus Christi the county seat of Nueces County?
faqs.a: Yes, according to the Handbook of Texas. City parcels are recorded at the Nueces County clerk's office.

faqs.q: Can I run a short-term rental in Corpus Christi?
faqs.a: Only with a registration permit. The city requires one for any rental under 30 days, and the rules have been under review, so ask Development Services which permit type applies and whether new ones are issued.

faqs.q: What happens to a rental permit when I sell?
faqs.a: Do not assume it carries over. Permits are issued annually and renewals face density rules, so get the city's answer before you describe the permit to a buyer.

faqs.q: Which date do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: February 1, for most bills. Penalty and interest start then, and the penalty rises monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: Do I need to keep hurricane repair records?
faqs.a: Keep them. Buyers, insurers and lenders often ask about past damage, and receipts back up your answers.
